newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt shares rise but may slip back - brokers.
newsitem.headline: Egypt shares rise but may slip back - brokers.

text.p: Egyptian share prices ended higher for the third consecutive day on Thursday but brokers warned investors that the market might have to slip a little before it could springboard to new levels.
The Capital Market Authority (CMA) overall index rose 2.69 points to 362.64 points, its highest level in almost 10 days. Volume was an average 47.97 million pounds ($14.13 million).
"It's definitely buying time at the market but investors have to be patient for a while. It's not a real uptrend," said broker Youssef Khalil of Delta EAB.

"Prices are certainly attractive but the market is not very stable and prices are expected to slip a little more before stabilising and then rising on solid ground," broker Sherif Cararah of EFG Hermes told Reuters.

Brokers said investor confidence in the market spurred an intensive buying spree in the first half of the session, but the price rally was dampened by investors offloading large blocks of shares at the new prices.
"There are still more sellers than buyers. When that is reversed, we'll see the real uptrend," Khalil said.
Brokers said shareholders dumped a lot of Upper Egypt Flour Mills stock, but some buying supported prices and the share ended 0.76 pounds down at 80.45 pounds.
The milling sector has seen lower prices after news that the private sector mills could prove tough competition for its the majority state-owned firms.

The cement and banking sector took the lion's share of trading. Helwan Portland Cement was the day's most active share, rising 1.99 to 74.5 pounds. Commercial International Bank/CIB came a close second in terms of turnover, but fell 0.31 to 72.70 pounds.

Investors were buying heavily into Kabo/Nasr Textiles and Clothing, a partially private firm in which the government has said it was willing to sell its majority holding. Kabo shares ended four pounds higher at 107 pounds.

PACHIN/Paints and Chemical Industries was also active on talk that the government would soon sell its holding in the firm through a global depositary receipt offering. Shares closed 1.50 pounds higher to 121.50 pounds.
The index for openly traded firms rose to 510.89 points from 509.39 points on Wednesday and that for the rarely traded "closed" firms also increased to 264.35 from 261.78 points.
Out of 90 shares traded, 38 rose and 27 fell while 23 ended unchanged.
